anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: Ex 3:14 the ever-one Name; holiness grasped in judgings/choosings/forsaking.
Imperative/optative; Ps 108 Judas; Tatian's 'God in darkness' refuted by Gen 1 jussives.
'We ourselves once had experience' — personal convert note.

choices.why: kephalaiōdēs = summing-up; a name compresses the whole proper quality — Origen's onomastics.
parekdochē = receiving amiss; Tatian took the imperative as optative-prayer — a taking-amiss with heretical fruit.

pass_a_gloss: 'Hallowed' presumes unhallowed: the name is God's proper quality (Ex 3:14 the one Name), and hallowing is our conception of him made holy across all his acts. Scripture's name-texts, psalm exaltation 'together' through shared divine power, and house-dedication ground the petition. Imperatives translate optatives; Tatian's impious inference (God prayed light because in darkness) collapses against the other creation jussives — a warning from Origen's own deceived past.
